Name: Great Pyramid of Cholula
Brief Description: Largest pyramid by volume in world (4.45M cubic meters), 300x315m base, built 3rd century BC-9th century AD, dedicated to Quetzalcoatl, with 5 miles of tunnels and church on top

Name: Church of Nuestra Señora de los Remedios
Brief Description: Baroque church atop Great Pyramid of Cholula, built by Spanish, symbol of religious conquest over pre-Hispanic temple

Name: Cerro de las Minas Archaeological Site
Brief Description: Ñuiñe Mixtec site (400-800 CE) north of Huajuapan de León, only extensively excavated lowland Mixtec site open to public, includes palaces, ball court, market, tombs

Name: Huajuapan de León Cathedral
Brief Description: Cathedral of Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, diocese seat since 1903, neoclassical style with 17th-19th century construction and modifications

Name: Capilla del Señor de los Corazones
Brief Description: 17th century chapel in Huajuapan, houses image of Lord of the Hearts credited with breaking 1812 siege during War of Independence

Name: Regional Museum of Huajuapan (MUREH)
Brief Description: Founded 1999, showcases Mixtec archaeology, ethnography and history with permanent and temporary exhibitions, library and artisan shop

Name: Cerro del Yukunitza Glass Lookout
Brief Description: Panoramic viewpoint overlooking Huajuapan de León, accessible via hiking trails with expansive valley views

Name: Monte Albán Archaeological Site
Brief Description: UNESCO World Heritage Zapotec capital (500 BCE-850 CE peak), 9km from Oaxaca, includes Great Plaza, ball court, observatory, tombs with frescoes

Name: Santo Domingo Church & Cultural Center
Brief Description: 17th century baroque masterpiece with gold leaf interior, adjacent museum with Monte Albán treasures, ethnobotanical garden, UNESCO area

Name: Oaxaca Historic Center (Zócalo)
Brief Description: UNESCO World Heritage colonial center, main plaza surrounded by portales, cafes, cathedral, and government palace

Name: Oaxaca Cathedral
Brief Description: Metropolitan Cathedral of Our Lady of the Assumption, baroque architecture with earthquake-resistant design, facing the zócalo

Name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre
Brief Description: Traditional covered market famous for tlayudas, tasajo (dried beef), mole, and authentic Oaxacan street food

Name: Mercado Benito Juárez
Brief Description: Artisan market adjacent to 20 de Noviembre, selling traditional crafts, textiles, mezcal, chocolate, local products

Name: Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca
Brief Description: Regional museum in former Santo Domingo monastery, 23 rooms covering Oaxacan history, Tomb 7 treasures from Monte Albán

Name: Textile Museum of Oaxaca
Brief Description: Museum dedicated to indigenous weaving traditions, natural dyes, and textile arts of Oaxaca's ethnic groups

Name: Ethnobotanical Garden
Brief Description: Behind Santo Domingo, showcases native Oaxacan plants with cultural significance, guided tours required, founded by Francisco Toledo

Name: Teotitlán del Valle
Brief Description: Traditional weaving village 31km from Oaxaca, hand-woven wool rugs with natural dyes, demonstrations and workshops available

Name: San Bartolo Coyotepec
Brief Description: Village 12km south famous for distinctive black pottery (barro negro), workshops and demonstrations available

Name: Santa María Atzompa
Brief Description: Village known for green-glazed ceramics and Day of the Dead cemetery celebrations, archaeological site nearby

Name: Mitla Archaeological Site
Brief Description: Zapotec site 44km from Oaxaca famous for intricate geometric stone mosaics, second most important site in Oaxaca state

Name: Santiago Matatlán
Brief Description: Self-proclaimed World Capital of Mezcal, 40% of Mexico's mezcal production, palenque tours and tastings available
